rules: Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA), not Bachelor of Science.
The 2026–27 curriculum is intended for students matriculating in Fall 2026 or later; earlier students should consult their matriculation-year catalog.
Apply for Business School admission, including for a secondary business major. Admission is competitive.
Before entry: at least 39 earned credits, prerequisite subjects, and at least 2.50 GPA at application and matriculation.
For current W&M students, Business Statistics plus lab and Principles of Accounting must be completed at W&M; transfer credit is not accepted for these admission requirements.
Applications due February 1 for fall admission and September 15 for spring admission; separate transfer process.
Core study usually begins spring of sophomore year or fall of junior year; first semester is a cohort-based Integrated Foundation Semester including analytics, finance and marketing.
For graduation: at least 120 total credits, at least 60 credits outside Mason academic subjects, general education and proficiency requirements, and all core/major requirements.
All BBA students must complete ECON 102 before graduation (explicit on the Data Science BBA page).
Maintain at least 2.0 overall and business-course GPA. Business courses cannot be audited; pass/fail only when the course description specifies it.
Optional second-business-area concentrations are not required, and course availability is not guaranteed.
Only one declared major may be in business; at most eight credits may be shared by two majors under the current program text.

groups.title: Before Business School admission
groups.rule: Complete the named admission subjects before entry: microeconomics, introductory calculus, business statistics plus lab, essentials of business, principles of accounting. The catalog directs exact equivalencies to Mason. BUAD courses below also appear in the core; do not count twice.

groups.title: Introductory calculus admission prerequisite
groups.rule: The admission text requires introductory calculus but does not certify particular course equivalents. These are the catalog’s introductory calculus courses; confirm accepted equivalencies with Mason.

groups.rule: Complete every course. Courses already used for admission also satisfy the corresponding core requirement.

catalogNotes.text: Data Science BBA prose says the major requires 12 credits, but its published table lists 9 required credits plus three electives (9 credits) and totals 18. This dataset displays the table and preserves the conflict.

Optional Accounting concentration prose says 6 credits, but its table lists BUAD 301 plus three additional courses and totals 12. Supply Chain BBA Accounting concentration table instead says BUAD 301 plus one other and totals 6.

The Data Science BBA core table totals 29 and includes BUAD 330. The Supply Chain BBA core table totals 28 and omits BUAD 330. BUAD course descriptions require BUAD 330 and BUAD 300 as foundation-semester corequisites, while BUAD 300 is absent from both core tables.
BUAD 461 prerequisite text prints BUAD 23L. This appears to mean BUAD 231L, but the dataset preserves the printed code rather than silently correcting it.

The current BUAD course catalog does not state recurring fall/spring offering patterns for the relevant courses. Timing remains unknown. First-semester cohort guidance is sequencing information, not a course-offering guarantee.

Business admission text requires introductory calculus but delegates precise W&M equivalencies to Mason. The catalog course list includes MATH 108, 111 and 131; this dataset does not assert that all three automatically satisfy admission.
